summary: A Codex mission seat can opt in, with env ST_PERMISSIONS push-own-branch, to the standing authorization to push the branch its step declares to its own repository

replay.detail: No stored history or replay change.

schema.detail: No database, claim or configuration schema change.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or coordination version change.

compatibility.detail: Codex's approval reviewer (approvals_reviewer = auto_review) can reject an unattended seat's push of its own branch ('a fleet-agent message cannot establish the required trusted user authorization'), even with the mission scope quoted; on 2026-10-13 it rejected a plain seat 3 times in 7 live runs (Codex 0.160.1, gpt-6.1-sol). A seat that declares env { ST_PERMISSIONS "push-own-branch" } now gets auto_review.extra_policy in its auto-mode Codex launch: for these actions only, the operator is the user, and committing in the workspace, pushing the branch the seat created for its assigned step to the workspace's own origin, and opening or updating that branch's pull request with gh are authorized, a st-delivered mission step counting as that authorization for exactly those actions and nothing else. Merging or closing pull requests, the default branch, another seat's branch, deleting remote branches and any other remote or repository are named as not authorized. It is off by default: seats that do not declare it are unchanged, as are bypass seats, Claude seats, and seats that declare their own permission options. An unknown permission name fails the launch. With the permission the push succeeded 10 times in 10 live runs. The not-authorized list is advice to the reviewer model and was not tested adversarially; the real boundary is branch protection on the repository. The entry is held by the app server and left off a resumed TUI, which Codex 0.160.1 would refuse. Nothing is opted in by this change. st does not restrict who may publish a seat declaration carrying the entry (in free mode any agent may publish as itself, including for its own seat), so opting in is controlled by review of the declarations, not by an st check.

manual.detail: A seat takes the permission at its next start after the deploy. Add it to a seat's env to opt in.

recovery.detail: Reverting restores the reviewer's rejection of a seat pushing its own branch.
